title: Rounding & estimation
examples: When do we need to round numbers?
What is the difference between rounding and estimating?
Can I round to a number that is not a multiple of ten?

explain.say: Today we are learning about rounding numbers. Rounding means finding a close, easy number. We round numbers to make them simpler to use.

items: Rounding finds a close, easy number.
We round numbers to simplify them.

explain.say: To round to the nearest ten, we look at the ones digit. If the ones digit is five or more, we round up. If it is four or less, we round down.
Let us round the number seventy-three to the nearest ten. The ones digit is three. Since three is less than five, we keep the tens digit the same. So, seventy-three rounds to seventy.

Next, we round one hundred twenty-eight to the nearest ten. The ones digit is eight. Since eight is five or more, we round up the tens digit. So, one hundred twenty-eight rounds to one hundred thirty.

We can also round to the nearest hundred. For example, round five hundred sixty-two to the nearest hundred. The tens digit is sixty. Since sixty is less than fifty, we round down. So, five hundred sixty-two rounds to five hundred.

faq.q: What is the difference between rounding and estimating?
faq.a: Rounding is finding a number that is close to the original number. Estimating is guessing a number that is close enough for a quick answer. Both help us check if our answer makes sense.
asks: Is estimating the same as rounding?
How do I check if my answer is reasonable?

faq.q: When do I need to use significant figures?
faq.a: We use significant figures when we want to keep an answer precise but not too long. It tells us how many digits in a number are important to the measurement. It is often used in science subjects.
asks: How many significant figures should I use?

faq.q: How do I round to the nearest thousand?
faq.a: To round to the nearest thousand, you look at the hundreds digit. If it is five or more, you round up the thousands digit. If it is four or less, you keep the thousands digit the same.
asks: What is the rule for rounding to thousands?
Should I look at the hundreds place when rounding to thousands?

faq.a: A decimal place is a number after the decimal point. It helps us show parts of a whole number. For example, zero point five is five tenths.
asks: What does the decimal point mean?
How many decimal places can I round to?

faq.q: If I round a number, do I have to change all the digits after the rounding spot?
faq.a: Yes, you must change all the digits after the rounding spot to zero. This shows that those places are now zero. For example, ninety-two becomes one hundred and zero.
asks: Do I write zeros when I round?
What happens to the digits after rounding?

facts: Rounding means finding a nearby, simpler number.
When rounding, you look at the digit immediately to the right of the place you are rounding to.
If the digit you look at is five or greater, you increase the rounding digit by one.
If the digit you look at is four or less, the rounding digit stays the same.

wrong.2: This is wrong because you should only round up if the tens digit is fifty or more.

quiz.say: Estimate the total of 58 and 23 by rounding to the nearest ten first.
quiz.why: Five eight rounds to sixty, and twenty three rounds to twenty ten. Sixty plus twenty ten equals eighty.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you rounded both numbers up too much.
wrong.1: This is wrong because rounding to the nearest ten gives you sixty and twenty ten, not seventy and thirty.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you must round both numbers before adding them together.
